title: The English Way
subtitle: A Pilgrim's Guide to the Camino Inglés
description_short: A calm, honest guide to the Camino Inglés: six walking days from Ferrol to Santiago, how the hundred-kilometre rule works, when to go, what to carry and how to arrive.
description_long:
The Camino Inglés is the short Camino: six walking days, about 113 km, from the naval city of Ferrol on the Galician coast to the cathedral of Santiago de Compostela. It follows the old way of the pilgrims who came by sea from Britain, Ireland and northern Europe, past estuaries, medieval bridges, Romanesque churches and the arcaded streets of Neda, Pontedeume and Betanzos, then over quiet hills and woodland to the Tambre and the last forest before the city.

This guide is written for the Planner first and the Walker's evenings second. It helps you decide whether this is your Camino, shape the walk, pack, and know what to check locally. It explains plainly how the hundred-kilometre rule for the Compostela works on this route, and why most pilgrims start in Ferrol rather than in A Coruña.

You will find a day-by-day account of the six stages, the shorter A Coruña variant, ways to split the long days, chapters on sleeping, eating and resting, on body, weather and safety, on the inner side of walking, and on arriving, with the Pilgrim's Office and the cathedral, and going home.

Every distance is marked approximate, and the book says where sources differ. It names no hostels, cafes or prices, because they change; it sends you to the CaminoPlus app and to local information for the live answer. Every fact in it is listed, with its source, in the book's fact ledger.
